prompt:
Implement `files/MigrationPlanClient.java` so that `MigrationPlanClient.buildPlan(...)` returns the ordered, machine-readable VCF migration architecture described by the supplied `files/estate-inventory.json`, `files/compatibility-snapshot.json`, and `files/installer-spec.json`. Produce an architecture artifact, not an explanatory report. Before implementing it, use your network research tools to consult current, real, reachable Broadcom-published sources for the supported migration paths, content and configuration compatibility, end-of-general-support boundaries, and the vSAN OSA/ESA host and networking implications; record the sources you actually consulted in the artifact. Do not treat the pinned snapshot as a substitute for that research: it is only the deterministic compatibility and sizing authority used by verification.

The returned JSON must conform exactly to the JSON Schema embedded in `installer-spec.json`. It must select and fully specify one of the OSA/ESA designs, including both evaluated options, host count, usable capacity, rack fit, hardware profile, and the required network changes. Place and size every target management component and supporting component listed by the pinned snapshot. For each inventoried source product, name its exact source product and version, target component and version, migration method and version path, end-of-support boundary, and give every inventoried content/configuration item exactly one `carry` or `abandon` disposition with a concrete action. Provide the ordered implementation steps and the technical gates for every step. Preserve genuine source choice: source records must describe what you consulted, but the verifier will not fetch them or require specific URLs or search queries.

Keep the implementation to the single client file. Do not modify `TestMain.java`, the installer specification, the estate fixture, or the pinned snapshot. You can verify the result with `javac files/MigrationPlanClient.java files/TestMain.java && java -cp files TestMain`.
